evidence_items.publisher: Reuters Institute for the Study of Journalism
evidence_items.locator: Introduction, survey limitations paragraph; frequency findings in Executive Summary and section 1
evidence_items.explanation: The March–April survey found low daily ChatGPT use, ranging from 1% in Japan to 7% in the United States, and considerable one-off experimentation. It supports limited routine use in those populations, but measures a snapshot rather than longitudinal retention.

evidence_items.publisher: McKinsey & Company; PDF hosted by ABBYY
evidence_items.locator: Page 4, section on adoption by business function
evidence_items.explanation: The February 22–March 5 survey reported that 65% of respondents’ organizations regularly used generative AI in at least one function. This challenges a blanket low-use account, but does not establish how long deployments lasted or represent every business.

unresolved_gaps: Neither survey follows the same adopters long enough to distinguish lasting adoption from recurring experimentation.
The consumer and business samples measure different populations and cannot be combined into a single adoption rate.
No representative retention or production-duration evidence settling the broad claim was retrieved.
